jobs.title: Director - Geological Data & Database Management
jobs.description:
Start Date: ASAP

Work Model: Hybrid

Location: Downtown Toronto

(outside Union Station – TTC & GO accessible)

Dress Code: Business Casual A Great Place to Work

Who We Are

Founded in 1993, Kinross is a Canadian-based senior gold mining company with operations and projects in the United States, Brazil, Mauritania, Chile and Canada. Our focus on delivering value is based on our four core values of Putting People First, Outstanding Corporate Citizenship, High Performance Culture, and Rigorous Financial Discipline.

Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC).

Job Summary

The Director, Geological Data & Database Management is a senior technical leadership role accountable for designing, implementing, and governing a company-wide database management system across all exploration, project, and operating sites. This is a hands-on leadership position: the Director is responsible for maintaining and updating company standards and ensuring sites adopt/adhere to them, ensuring standardization of database software and structures across all sites, and building and managing a team of database administrators and analysts.

Key Responsibilities

Ensure standardization of the company geologic database platform across all exploration, project, and operating sites, including migration of legacy and existing site databases where required.
Maintain database standards for structure, content, and required tables at each project maturity point (Setup, Initial Drilling, Infill, Scoping, PFS, FS, and Operations), and ensure sites are equipped to meet them.
Lead selection, configuration, and lifecycle management of database software and related tools, in partnership with IT.
Ensure QA/QC protocols are implemented and auditable per internal standards.
Establish and audit data security controls across all sites: layered/restricted access by user type, edit tracking and audit trails, and automatic, regular backups including offsite storage.
Define and enforce the separation between dynamic project databases and frozen, dated resource-model databases used for reserve/resource work.
Lead systematic, scheduled reviews of database quality across all sites and drive corrective action plans ahead of each project maturity point.
Initiate and lead internal and external audits as required.
Build, lead, and develop the company database management function, including hiring and mentoring site and project database administrators and analysts.
liase with exploration management, KTS, and site geology teams to ensure database structures support geological, resource, and reserve modelling requirements.
Develop and deliver training and documented procedures for database administrators, geologists, and technical staff on data entry standards, QA/QC execution, and system use.
Maintain and continuously improve governing documentation (standards guides, database structure references.)
Report on database health, compliance, and risk to senior technical and executive leadership.

Qualifications And Skills

Education and Experience

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Earth Sciences, Geological Engineering, or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in mineral exploration or mining geology, including significant experience in geological database design, administration, or data management.
5+ years in a senior or leadership role managing database systems, technical teams, or data governance programs across multiple sites or projects.
Demonstrated experience implementing or administering industry-standard geological database platforms (e.g., acQuire, Fusion, Datashed, or comparable systems) at a multi-site scale.

Technical & Leadership Skills

Deep understanding of relational database structures as applied to drill hole data (collar, survey, lithology, assay, QA/QC, geotechnical, geometallurgical, density, and related tables).
Strong knowledge of QA/QC protocols, chain-of-custody procedures, and data security/access-control best practices in a geological or mining context.
Proven ability to lead large-scale systems and change management initiatives across geographically distributed sites.
Excellent people-leadership skills, with experience building and managing teams, including remote or site-based staff and dotted-line reporting relationships.
Strong communication skills, able to translate technical database requirements for both site-level technical staff and executive leadership.
Willingness and ability to travel regularly to exploration, project, and operating sites, including remote locations.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary range for this role is $180,000 to $220,000 CAD plus a target Short-Term Incentive bonus of 30%, 30% (LTI) and group benefit coverage. The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate’s experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development.

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

jobs.description:
Type:
In-Office | Full-Time, Permanent

About Our Client

Our client is a well-established and growing Alberta-based organization with a diverse portfolio of operations and a reputation for innovation, operational excellence, and long-term strategic growth.
The organization has made significant investments in enterprise systems, technology, and business transformation and is now focused on advancing the next stage of its digital evolution.
Reporting to a senior executive leader, this role offers the opportunity to shape enterprise technology strategy, strengthen data and cybersecurity capabilities, lead artificial intelligence initiatives, and support business growth through technology, innovation, and systems thinking. The successful candidate will play a critical role in connecting people, processes, data, technology, and business outcomes across a complex and evolving organization.

Key Responsibilities

As the Vice President, Information Technology
, you will serve as the organization's senior-most technology leader, accountable for the strategy, security, performance, and continued evolution of the systems, data, and digital capabilities that support the business. You will lead enterprise technology initiatives, oversee the internal IT function, manage key technology partners, and ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value.

Enterprise Leadership, Systems Thinking & Innovation
Contribute technology, data, cybersecurity, and innovation perspectives to enterprise planning and strategic decision-making.
Apply systems thinking to evaluate the impact of technology decisions across business units, processes, data flows, risks, and customer outcomes.
Identify opportunities to improve scalability, efficiency, integration, and organizational performance.
Support growth initiatives, business expansion, and future strategic opportunities through technology leadership.

IT Strategy & Digital Transformation
Develop, execute, and continuously evolve a multi-year enterprise technology roadmap aligned with organizational priorities.
Lead digital transformation initiatives that simplify work, improve integration, automate processes, and enhance business performance.
Establish governance practices for technology investments, prioritization, funding, and benefits realization.
Drive technology change management, adoption, and organizational readiness for new systems and capabilities.

Enterprise Systems, Architecture & ERP Leadership
Serve as the executive owner of the organization's enterprise application ecosystem and integration architecture.
Oversee the lifecycle, integration, optimization, and governance of enterprise platforms and business-critical systems.
Establish enterprise architecture principles that support scalability, reliability, interoperability, and security.
Lead major software selection, implementation, optimization, and retirement initiatives from planning through stabilization.

Artificial Intelligence, Data & Analytics
Develop and lead the organization's enterprise artificial intelligence strategy and governance framework.
Identify practical, high-value opportunities for AI, advanced analytics, and automation across the business.
Establish enterprise data governance standards, including data ownership, stewardship, quality, and reporting practices.
Strengthen reporting and analytics capabilities to support informed decision-making throughout the organization.

Cybersecurity, Privacy, Risk & Business Continuity
Provide executive leadership for cybersecurity, information security governance, privacy, and technology risk management.
Oversee policies, controls, monitoring, identity and access management, backup, disaster recovery, and incident response practices.
Maintain technology and cybersecurity risk mitigation programs and business continuity plans.
Communicate technology, security, privacy, and vendor risks to Executive leadership in clear business terms.

Managed Service Provider & Vendor Management
Act as the executive point of accountability for outsourced technology service providers and strategic technology vendors.
Define service expectations, governance practices, key performance metrics, and escalation processes.
Lead contract negotiations, renewals, major technology purchases, and vendor due diligence activities.
Ensure technology partners deliver strong service, accountability, security, and value.

Team Leadership & Development
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing IT team.
Balance operational reliability with strategic initiatives, project delivery, governance, and innovation.
Support workforce development through coaching, succession planning, training, and professional development initiatives.
Foster a collaborative, service-oriented, and business-minded team culture.

Financial & Project Stewardship
Develop and manage annual technology operating and capital budgets.
Build business cases that support technology investments and strategic initiatives.
Monitor project performance, technology spending, implementation outcomes, and return on investment.
Ensure initiatives are delivered with clear governance, accountability, and measurable success criteria.

Business Partnership & Organizational Change
Serve as the primary technology advisor to Executive leadership and business stakeholders.
Translate business needs into technology, process, data, and change solutions.
Build alignment across departments and facilitate shared ownership of enterprise initiatives.
Promote adoption of new capabilities through communication, training, and stakeholder engagement.

Qualifications

To succeed in this role, candidates should demonstrate the following:

Education & Experience
Degree or diploma in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Management Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related discipline. Equivalent experience will be considered.
Minimum 12 years of progressive Information Technology experience, including substantial leadership experience at the Director, Vice President, CIO, or comparable executive level.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise technology strategy within complex, multi-entity, or multi-business-unit environments.
Proven experience leading enterprise application portfolios and major ERP or enterprise software implementations from selection through stabilization.
Experience managing outsourced technology services, strategic vendors, and major technology investments.
Experience leading digital transformation, cybersecurity programs, data governance initiatives, business continuity planning, and enterprise technology governance.
Experience in real estate development, homebuilding, construction, or another project- and asset-based industry is strongly preferred.

Technical Skills
Strong expertise in enterprise systems, integration architecture, digital transformation, cybersecurity, cloud technologies, data governance, automation, reporting, and artificial intelligence.
Experience overseeing enterprise technology ecosystems, application portfolios, and complex technology environments.
Knowledge of enterprise governance frameworks, technology risk management, vendor management, and business continuity practices.
Relevant certifications such as PMP, CISSP, CISM, COBIT, ITIL, or recognized AI governance credentials are considered assets.

jobs.title: Director Inclusion - Data, Insights & Operations
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

The People, Culture and Talent team helps shape the experiences that support our people, our culture and our workplace so we can help make our clients’ ambitions a reality. As Director, Inclusion - Data, Insights and Operations, you’ll lead the data, reporting, financial management and business operations activities that support the execution of CIBC’s enterprise Inclusion strategy. You’ll build and manage analytics, dashboards, scorecards and performance measures that help leaders understand progress, identify opportunities and make informed decisions. You’ll partner across Human Resources and business teams to translate workforce and portfolio data into clear, actionable insights and reporting. You’ll also oversee budget planning and financial management for the Inclusion portfolio, strengthen reporting routines and controls, and drive continuous improvement. In this leadership role, you’ll help create a more integrated, measurable and effective approach to advancing inclusion across the enterprise.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Lead analytics and reporting - Develop, implement and manage Inclusion analytics, dashboards, scorecards and key performance indicators that measure progress against enterprise priorities and commitments.
Generate actionable insights - Translate workforce, demographic and portfolio data into clear trends, risks and opportunities, and provide recommendations that support decision-making and continuous improvement.
Strengthen operational excellence - Establish and maintain reporting routines, planning mechanisms, controls and governance practices that support consistent execution, accountability and effective delivery across the Inclusion portfolio.
Manage financial performance - Lead budget administration, forecasting, expense tracking, reconciliations and reporting for the Inclusion portfolio, ensuring strong financial discipline and alignment with business priorities.
Collaborate across partners - Work closely with Human Resources, Legal, Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG), and business leaders to support reporting requirements, submissions, planning activities and enterprise priorities.
Lead and develop the team - Provide caring, accountable leadership that inspires strong performance, builds team capability and supports an inclusive, high-performing environment.

Who You Are

You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems and making sense of information. You communicate detailed information in a meaningful way.
You look beyond the moment. You think strategically and can translate long-term priorities into practical action plans, measurable outcomes and sustainable change across the bank.
Your influence makes a difference. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by sharing your expertise.
You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and implementing strategic team goals. You have experience coaching employees and inspiring successful team performance.
You can demonstrate experience in analytics, reporting, key performance indicator development, financial management, budget forecasting, and executive-level presentation development.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

jobs.description:
“Join us in
building Careers and shaping Experiences Beyond the Box”

About Us

At Atlantic Packaging, every box tells a story and yours begins here. As a proudly Canadian-owned company with over 80 years of excellence in the corrugated packaging industry with operations within North America (Ontario, Quebec and United States), we’re committed to sustainability, customer excellence and community impact. Since 1945, we’ve supported local jobs and built a legacy of trust with our clients and team members. At Atlantic, your ideas matter, your growth is supported and your work makes a real impact.

The Opportunity

The Director of Planning & Inventory will lead the Ontario Corrugated team’s supply and inventory planning function to ensure customers receive their desired product at the service level they expect. Reporting to the Vice President of Supply Chain & Strategy, this role is critical for building organizational planning capability to support sustainable, profitable growth. It ensures alignment between business strategy and operational execution across production, procurement, and distribution.

The Director of Planning & Inventory leads a team of managers, planners and analysts with a focus on driving structure, establishing best practices for planning tools and processes, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to enhance forecast accuracy, machine utilization, inventory efficiency, and overall supply chain responsiveness.

What You’ll Do

Oversee the development and execution of the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP/IBP) process, ensuring alignment between demand, capacity, and financial plans across the organization
Direct inventory strategy to balance customer service levels with working capital objectives, minimizing excess/obsolete stock while preventing stockouts
Oversee supply planning and production scheduling alignment, ensuring plans reflect realistic capacity, lead times, and material availability
Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing planning team, including senior managers, plant-floor schedulers and inventory analysts
Partner with Sales and Business Performance teams to ensure the demand forecast can be utilized most effectively for capacity planning
Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Finance, Mills, and Sales to resolve supply-demand imbalances and support integrated business decision-making
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) — including forecast accuracy, scheduling compliance, inventory turns, fill rate, and on-time in full delivery — and drive corrective action where targets are not met
Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance planning maturity, process efficiency, and responsiveness to demand volatility
Provide senior leadership with visibility into planning risks, opportunities, and trade-offs to support strategic decision-making

What You Bring

The ideal candidate brings strong analytical and leadership skills, deep expertise in demand and supply planning methodologies, and a track record of driving results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Required

Undergraduate degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field
Certificate in Supply Chain Management considered an asset; APICS/ASCM,CPIM, CSCP or CPF
Experience building tools in PowerBI considered an asset
8+ years of progressive experience in demand planning, supply planning, or inventory management, including 3–5+ years in a leadership role
Strong track-record of developing high-performing teams while overseeing day-to-day operations
Proven experience leading S&OP/IBP processes in a manufacturing environment
Proven experience in improving capacity/demand planning processes, inventory efficiency, and service levels in a complex, fast-paced environment
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Excellent analytical skills with an ability to manipulate large data sets and present analyses in a clear, concise manner
Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate data into actionable business insights for various groups of stakeholders
Demonstrated continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify metrics related to business processes, improving results through effective processes
Demonstrated proficiency in time management

What We Offer

Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage (dependents included)
Teamwork-focused culture with sustainability initiatives and social events
A culture of appreciation through a point-based recognition
Opportunities for advancement and internal movement
Education assistance for continuous skill development
Academic scholarships for employees’ children
Safety equipment and PPE support program
Retirement savings and wellness initiatives
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Inclusion and Accessibility

Atlantic Packaging is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible and respectful environment for all candidates. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, please contact our Talent Acquisition team—we’re here to support you.

We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest in joining Atlantic Packaging. While we appreciate the time and effort invested, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please note

Candidates who are 18 years or older are required to complete a criminal and background check. Details will be provided through the application process.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Location: Vancouver HQ (hybrid), with operations in Alberta, Ontario and Quebec 

Compensation: $300,000 - $380,000 CAD base + performance bonus + stock options

Who We Are

Fresh Prep is Canada's largest Canadian-owned meal kit company and a certified B Corporation. We deliver chef-created meal kits, prepared meals and a growing grocery marketplace to customers across the country, from production facilities in British Columbia, Alberta, and Quebec, with operations in Ontario. We're a team of over 600 people and over $110M in annual revenue.

Our founders were named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 winners and we've been recognized as one of Deloitte's Best Managed Companies in Canada, one of BC's Top Employers, and one of Globe and Mail's Top Growing Companies.

The Role
You'll own the financial function of a national, multi-province, physical-operations business with subscription economics, which means you need to be fluent in both cohort and contribution margin analysis and in the operating systems required to manage food costs, labour productivity, last mile delivery and freight. 

You'll be accountable for the numbers the Board and our Investors see, capital strategy and the financial rigour that lets the executive team make decisions quickly and correctly.

You'll report to the CEO, sit on the executive team, and be a standing presence in the boardroom. You will also, at points, be the person telling the rest of us that something we want to do doesn't work. We're looking for someone who is comfortable doing that.

What You'll Be DoingFinancial leadership and reporting

Own all financial reporting, including GAAP compliant statements, the annual audit and consolidated reporting across multiple provinces and legal entities.

Own internal management reporting and commentary that gives the executive team and Board timely insight into trends, unit economics, and the drivers behind them: not just what happened, but why.

Own the operating and capital budget process and hold the company to it.

Own the financial metrics framework across the business, including cohort retention, margin, customer payback and facility-level unit economics.

Capital, cash, and financing

Own cash management, working capital, and cash forecasting in a business with meaningful inventory and seasonality.

Manage our lending relationships, credit facilities, and covenant compliance.

Lead financing strategy and execution: debt, asset-based and project finance, equity, and government programs, in partnership with the CEO and founders.

Manage reporting and communication to a capital structure that includes multiple classes of equity and institutional investors, including the obligations that come with it.

Own the government funding agenda, including SR&ED and applicable federal and provincial grant programs.

Transactions and strategic projects

Lead financial diligence, modelling, and integration on acquisitions and other strategic transactions. 

Provide modelling and analytical support for growth decisions: new facilities, capacity investment, category expansion, long-term supply contracts, and technology investment.

Bring financial discipline to pricing and promotional strategy in partnership with the CMO, including the margin envelope within which marketing operates.

Operations partnership

Own cost accounting for a manufacturing and logistics business: standard costs, food cost variance, labour productivity, delivery, freight, and waste.

Partner with Operations on the decisions that determine our gross margin and be a genuine second set of eyes on capital projects.

Support technology and automation decisions with credible business cases and honest post-mortems.

Compliance and governance

Ensure legal and regulatory compliance across all financial functions, including multi-province tax (GST/HST, QST, PST), payroll compliance in four provinces including Quebec, and corporate filings.

Maintain the internal controls appropriate to our scale and to the diligence standards our investors and lenders apply.

Support the Board and its committees with materials, forecasts, and the analysis behind major decisions.

Team

Lead, structure, and develop the finance, accounting and supply chain teams

Continue building systems and processes that create more thinking and less data manipulation. This is a company where the finance team should be spending its time on analysis, not on reconciliation.

What We're Looking For
Required

12+ years in finance and/or accounting, including senior finance leadership in a company at or above $75M in revenue.

CPA designation, with a degree in accounting, finance, or business.

Experience in physical-operations businesses: manufacturing, food production, CPG, or logistics, including hands-on cost accounting ownership.

Demonstrated ownership of an external audit and GAAP reporting.

Experience securing debt financing and managing lender relationships and covenants.

Experience with a modern ERP environment and ancillary tech-stack.

Multi-site operating experience in a manufacturing environment.

Strongly preferred

M&A experience with due diligence, deal structuring and integration integration 

Experience with subscription or recurring-revenue economics alongside physical operations.

Experience with institutional equity investors

Experience preparing a company for a liquidity or capital event.

SR&ED and government grant program experience.

How you work

You reason from data and are honest about what the data doesn't tell you.

You can explain complex financial concepts to a room of operators without either condescending or losing them.

You build environments where other people do their best work, and you develop people rather than accumulating tasks.

You are fluent with AI tooling and actively use it in your own work. Not as a talking point, but because you've found it makes your analysis faster and your team's time better spent. You have a view on where it belongs in a finance function and where it doesn't.

You are willing to be the dissenting voice, and you know how to disagree without being obstructive.

You can toggle between daily finance tasks and strategic board conversations comfortably and can operate with precision in both.

You don’t have an ego, you don’t need to be right and you are happy as long as the decision helps achieve the company’s goals.

What You Can Expect

Competitive executive compensation, performance bonus, and participation in our Employee Stock Option Plan.

Hybrid work, with our HQ in East Vancouver.

Comprehensive executive health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance.

A Fresh Prep meal plan

A highly impactful seat at the table of a Canadian company that is at the forefront of food innovation 

Fresh Prep is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination of any kind. We value diversity at every level of the company and aim to be representative of the communities we operate in. We endeavour to recruit, develop, and retain the best talent from a diverse candidate pool, and we believe diversity, equity, and inclusion among our team is vital to our success.

jobs.description:
En tant que Leader de pratique en stratégie de l'intelligence artificielle, vous jouez un rôle clé au sein du bureau du chef des données et intelligence artificielle, en accompagnant les différents secteurs de l’organisation dans la génération, la priorisation et la mise en œuvre de leurs initiatives en analytique et en intelligence artificielle (IA). Votre mandat consiste à aider les équipes à tirer pleinement profit des données et de l’intelligence artificielle pour atteindre leurs objectifs d’affaires. Pour ce faire, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires d’affaires afin de bien comprendre leurs enjeux, d’identifier les opportunités et d’aligner les efforts analytiques sur les priorités stratégiques de l’organisation. Avec les secteurs, vous menez des démarches de recensement des opportunités à partir des processus d’affaires et contribuez aux réflexions sur leur transformation par l’IA. jobs.title: Director, Strategy and Corporate Development
jobs.description:
Req Id:
432851

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell AI Fabric is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform. As Director, Strategic Finance & Corporate Development, you will work at the centre of Bell AI Fabric's most important investment, capital allocation, commercial, and growth decisions, providing the financial insight and execution discipline required to scale the business.

This is a highly visible, hands-on finance role with unusual breadth and access. Working directly with senior executives, the Bell AI Fabric Board, Bell Finance leadership, and business teams, you will lead business cases, financial modelling, capital planning, performance analysis, and finance support for major customer, partnership, and infrastructure opportunities.

You will turn complex operational, commercial, tax, and accounting inputs into clear financial conclusions and decision-ready materials. You will also manage and develop team members, set priorities, review work closely, and raise the quality, precision, and pace of the team's output.

This is a unique opportunity for a finance, consulting, investment banking, or corporate development professional who wants to help build something consequential and expand their responsibilities quickly. You do not need to arrive knowing every aspect of the business. Success will come from curiosity, sound judgment, humility, exceptional care in the work, and a willingness to invest the effort required to learn and figure things out.

Key Responsibilities

Act as a trusted strategic finance partner to the executive team, leading the financial analysis behind Bell AI Fabric's highest-priority investments, commercial opportunities, and growth initiatives.
Build, maintain, and drive integrated financial models, business cases, forecasts, sensitivities, and decision tools that connect customer demand, pricing, capacity, capital requirements, operating costs, tax, accounting, and expected returns.
Lead monthly and quarterly capital allocation processes, assess competing requirements, challenge assumptions, and recommend how capital should be prioritized across projects and opportunities.
Question business stakeholders constructively and use judgment to reconcile commercial ambition, financial discipline, operational realities, risk, and timing into the best overall financial decision.
Support major customer opportunities, partnerships, financing initiatives, and transactions through rigorous economics, scenario analysis, financial diligence, and executive recommendations, while partnering with the deal lead on negotiations and structuring.
Work closely with Tax, Accounting, Treasury, FP&A, Corporate Development, and project teams to ensure financial conclusions reflect the appropriate treatment, assumptions, controls, and enterprise requirements.
Translate financial priorities into executable workplans with clear outputs, owners, milestones, dependencies, review points, and escalation paths; drive workstreams through completion.
Identify and improve financial processes, governance, model controls, reporting, and decision-support capabilities as Bell AI Fabric scales.

Critical Qualifications

Typically 6-10 years of experience in strategic finance, corporate development, investment banking, management consulting, FP&A, project finance, accounting, or another environment that develops comparable financial and execution capabilities.
Strong financial modelling capability, including experience building integrated models, business cases, forecasts, sensitivities, and scenario analyses that support significant decisions.
Demonstrated ability to review complex models and analyses with precision, identify errors or unsupported assumptions, and improve the quality and clarity of the underlying work.
Strong PowerPoint, executive communication, and financial storytelling skills, with the ability to translate complex concepts into clean, decision-oriented materials for senior executives and the Bell AI Fabric Board.
Sound financial and commercial judgment, with the confidence to question stakeholders, pressure-test assumptions, and recommend a practical path forward.
Working knowledge of tax, accounting, and financial reporting considerations, and the ability to partner effectively with subject-matter experts.
Experience managing or developing others, setting clear expectations, reviewing work closely, and maintaining accountability without creating unnecessary hierarchy.
High capacity and exceptional attention to detail, with the ability to work quickly across multiple urgent priorities without compromising accuracy or quality.
Ability to operate independently, navigate ambiguity, learn unfamiliar topics quickly, and invest additional effort during critical periods to reach a well-supported answer.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA, CFA, or equivalent financial designations or advanced finance training; candidates with strong equivalent experience are also encouraged to apply.
Experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, investments, partnerships, due diligence, valuation, integration planning, or other transaction-related work.
Experience in infrastructure, technology, telecommunications, energy, data centres, project finance, or another capital-intensive industry.
Advanced Excel and financial modelling skills, with disciplined model structure, documentation, version control, and quality assurance.
Strong curiosity and a demonstrated ability to become credible quickly on unfamiliar commercial, technical, tax, and accounting topics.
A practical, collaborative, and low-ego working style, including comfort receiving challenge, changing course when the facts require it, and sharing credit with the team.
High standards for pace, precision, ownership, accountability, and follow-through, combined with a genuine interest in difficult problems and continuous learning.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

Additional Information

Management

Regular - Full Time

Canada : Ontario : Toronto

10/15/2026

For work arrangements that are ‘Hybrid’, successful candidates must be based in Canada and report to a set Bell office for a minimum of 3 days a week. Recognizing the importance of work-life balance, Bell offers flexibility in work hours based on the business needs.

Please apply directly online to be considered for this role. Applications through email will not be accepted.

We know that caring for our team members is at the heart of a healthy, positive and thriving workplace. As part of our team, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive compensation package that includes a competitive salary and a wide range of benefits to support the well-being of you and your family. As soon as you join us, you'll be eligible for medical, dental, vision and mental health benefits that you can tailor to your specific needs. Plus, as a Bell team member, you'll enjoy a 35% discount on our services and access exclusive offers from our partners.

At Bell, we are proud of our focus on fostering an inclusive and accessible workplace where all team members feel valued, respected, supported, and that they belong.

Bell is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise. We also want to make sure that everyone has an equal opportunity to join our team. We encourage individuals who may require accommodations during the hiring process to let us know. For a confidential inquiry, email your recruiter or recruitment@bell.ca to make arrangements. If you have questions or feedback regarding accessibility at Bell, we invite you to complete the Accessibility feedback form or visit our Accessibility page for other ways to contact us.

Artificial intelligence may be used to assess parts of your application. Please review our privacy policy (see Phenom for details) to learn more about how we collect, use, and disclose your personal information.

jobs.title: AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition and Readiness
jobs.description:
Manulife Canada is transforming how operational work is received, processed, routed, completed and measured across servicing functions. This includes retiring legacy workflow platforms, re-engineering operational processes, modernizing technology architecture, and introducing reusable AI-enabled automation capabilities that improve service, strengthen controls, and create a more scalable operating model. This position will help lead the transformation program supporting this vision while establishing reusable business and technology capabilities that can be applied across future modernization initiatives.

The AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition & Readiness will play a pivotal leadership role in one of Manulife Canada's largest operational transformation programs. The successful candidate will be accountable for integrated program delivery, transition management, operational readiness, release governance, and execution of the legacy workflow system retirement roadmap across multiple transformation waves.

This role sits at the intersection of operations, technology and delivery. The successful candidate will ensure business capabilities are deployed safely, the organization is prepared to operate through interim states, and transformation outcomes are successfully scaled across the enterprise.

Position Responsibilities

The AVP, Transformation Delivery, Transition & Readiness is accountable for planning, coordinating, governing and executing the transformation roadmap. The role leads the Program Management Office while also establishing the transition strategies, release governance, readiness practices and operating-model controls required to move the organization from current-state operations to future-state operations. The role owns delivery execution and operational implementation of the transformation.

Program and Portfolio Delivery

Own the integrated transformation roadmap.
Govern program schedules, milestones and delivery commitments.
Manage critical path dependencies and inter-workstream coordination.
Lead program governance forums and executive reporting.
Establish delivery performance measures and escalation mechanisms.
Maintain integrated views of scope, timeline, financials and risks.

PMO Leadership

Lead and develop the Program Management Office.
Establish governance processes, standards and controls.
Manage executive reporting, dashboards, status reviews and Steering Committee materials.
Oversee RAID management and dependency tracking.
Coordinate planning across business, technology and delivery workstreams.

Transition Management

Develop the enterprise transition strategy for workflow system retirement.
Define interim-state operating models and deployment approaches.
Establish coexistence strategies for legacy and future-state environments.
Coordinate cutover and rollout planning across business units.
Manage hypercare, stabilization and post-deployment support activities.
Ensure operational continuity throughout transformation waves.

Operational Readiness

Define operational readiness frameworks and checkpoints.
Establish release-level go-live criteria.
Coordinate readiness assessments across business and technology stakeholders.
Ensure operational support models are established and sustainable.
Govern release approvals and deployment decision processes.

Integration Readiness & Ecosystem Coordination

Govern cross-platform dependency management.
Coordinate ecosystem readiness activities across impacted applications.
Track platform onboarding, retirement and transition activities.
Monitor system integration risks impacting rollout schedules.
Partner with Architecture, Engineering and Technology leaders to establish release readiness.
Govern temporary bridge solutions required during transformation waves.

Workflow System Retirement Execution

Maintain workflow system retirement execution plan.
Track retirement dependencies and readiness criteria.
Coordinate enterprise-wide retirement planning activities.
Ensure all retirement risks are identified and managed.
Support final platform decommissioning and transition activities.

Required Qualifications

10+ years leading large-scale enterprise transformation programs.
Experience managing multi-year technology and operations transformation initiatives.
Proven track record establishing PMO and governance functions.
Experience executing phased technology migrations and platform retirements.
Strong understanding of operational readiness, deployment management and transition planning.
Experience managing third-party delivery partners and systems integrators.
Financial services, insurance or operations transformation experience preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with AWD or a comparable workflow platform, such as Pega, Appian, or FileNet, at scale.
Experience establishing reusable automation components or shared engineering services across business units.
Experience delivering transformation in a federally regulated financial institution, including familiarity with OSFI expectations for change and outsourcing.

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Financial Officer

Fresh Prep Foods Inc.

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer
Location: Vancouver HQ (hybrid), with operations in Alberta, Ontario and Quebec
Compensation: $300,000 - $380,000 CAD base + performance bonus + stock options

Who We Are

Fresh Prep is Canada's largest Canadian-owned meal kit company and a certified B Corporation. We deliver chef-created meal kits, prepared meals and a growing grocery marketplace to customers across the country, from production facilities in British Columbia, Alberta, and Quebec, with operations in Ontario. We're a team of over 600 people and over $110M in annual revenue.
Our founders were named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 winners and we've been recognized as one of Deloitte's Best Managed Companies in Canada, one of BC's Top Employers, and one of Globe and Mail's Top Growing Companies.

The Role

You'll own the financial function of a national, multi-province, physical-operations business with subscription economics, which means you need to be fluent in both cohort and contribution margin analysis and in the operating systems required to manage food costs, labour productivity, last mile delivery and freight.
You'll be accountable for the numbers the Board and our Investors see, capital strategy and the financial rigour that lets the executive team make decisions quickly and correctly.
You'll report to the CEO, sit on the executive team, and be a standing presence in the boardroom. You will also, at points, be the person telling the rest of us that something we want to do doesn't work. We're looking for someone who is comfortable doing that.

What You'll Be Doing

Financial leadership and reporting

Own all financial reporting, including GAAP compliant statements, the annual audit and consolidated reporting across multiple provinces and legal entities.
Own internal management reporting and commentary that gives the executive team and Board timely insight into trends, unit economics, and the drivers behind them: not just what happened, but why.
Own the operating and capital budget process and hold the company to it.
Own the financial metrics framework across the business, including cohort retention, margin, customer payback and facility-level unit economics.

Capital, cash, and financing

Own cash management, working capital, and cash forecasting in a business with meaningful inventory and seasonality.
Manage our lending relationships, credit facilities, and covenant compliance.
Lead financing strategy and execution: debt, asset-based and project finance, equity, and government programs, in partnership with the CEO and founders.
Manage reporting and communication to a capital structure that includes multiple classes of equity and institutional investors, including the obligations that come with it.
Own the government funding agenda, including SR&ED and applicable federal and provincial grant programs.

Transactions and strategic projects

Lead financial diligence, modelling, and integration on acquisitions and other strategic transactions.
Provide modelling and analytical support for growth decisions: new facilities, capacity investment, category expansion, long-term supply contracts, and technology investment.
Bring financial discipline to pricing and promotional strategy in partnership with the CMO, including the margin envelope within which marketing operates.

Operations partnership

Own cost accounting for a manufacturing and logistics business: standard costs, food cost variance, labour productivity, delivery, freight, and waste.
Partner with Operations on the decisions that determine our gross margin and be a genuine second set of eyes on capital projects.
Support technology and automation decisions with credible business cases and honest post-mortems.

Compliance and governance

Ensure legal and regulatory compliance across all financial functions, including multi-province tax (GST/HST, QST, PST), payroll compliance in four provinces including Quebec, and corporate filings.
Maintain the internal controls appropriate to our scale and to the diligence standards our investors and lenders apply.
Support the Board and its committees with materials, forecasts, and the analysis behind major decisions.

Team

Lead, structure, and develop the finance, accounting and supply chain teams
Continue building systems and processes that create more thinking and less data manipulation. This is a company where the finance team should be spending its time on analysis, not on reconciliation.

What We're Looking For

Required

12+ years in finance and/or accounting, including senior finance leadership in a company at or above $75M in revenue.
CPA designation, with a degree in accounting, finance, or business.
Experience in physical-operations businesses: manufacturing, food production, CPG, or logistics, including hands-on cost accounting ownership.
Demonstrated ownership of an external audit and GAAP reporting.
Experience securing debt financing and managing lender relationships and covenants.
Experience with a modern ERP environment and ancillary tech-stack.
Multi-site operating experience in a manufacturing environment.

Strongly preferred

M&A experience with due diligence, deal structuring and integration
Experience with subscription or recurring-revenue economics alongside physical operations.
Experience with institutional equity investors
Experience preparing a company for a liquidity or capital event.
SR&ED and government grant program experience.

How you work

You reason from data and are honest about what the data doesn't tell you.
You can explain complex financial concepts to a room of operators without either condescending or losing them.
You build environments where other people do their best work, and you develop people rather than accumulating tasks.
You are fluent with AI tooling and actively use it in your own work. Not as a talking point, but because you've found it makes your analysis faster and your team's time better spent. You have a view on where it belongs in a finance function and where it doesn't.
You are willing to be the dissenting voice, and you know how to disagree without being obstructive.
You can toggle between daily finance tasks and strategic board conversations comfortably and can operate with precision in both.
You don’t have an ego, you don’t need to be right and you are happy as long as the decision helps achieve the company’s goals.

What You Can Expect

Competitive executive compensation, performance bonus, and participation in our Employee Stock Option Plan.
Hybrid work, with our HQ in East Vancouver.
Comprehensive executive health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance.
A Fresh Prep meal plan
A highly impactful seat at the table of a Canadian company that is at the forefront of food innovation

Fresh Prep is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination of any kind. We value diversity at every level of the company and aim to be representative of the communities we operate in. We endeavour to recruit, develop, and retain the best talent from a diverse candidate pool, and we believe diversity, equity, and inclusion among our team is vital to our success.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Strategy
jobs.description:
Are you a strategic finance leader who thrives in a collaborative, evolving environment and is passionate about using financial insight to support organizational impact? Canada’s National Ballet School (NBS) is excited to invite applications for the position of Director of Financial Strategy. This is an exciting opportunity to provide strategic financial leadership, strengthen enterprise-wide decision-making, and help shape the continued evolution of NBS’ Finance function.

About Us

Canada’s National Ballet School (NBS) is a leading arts and education institution dedicated to excellence in dance training, community programming, and health initiatives. NBS has 300+ employees supporting programs ranging from professional ballet training and community engagement to groundbreaking health initiatives. NBS fosters a collaborative, creative environment rooted in inclusion and continuous growth.

The Role

Reporting to the Chief Strategy and Operations Officer (CSOO) and working closely with the Executive Director and Artistic Director, the Director of Financial Strategy is a key member of NBS’ Senior Management team. This role provides strategic leadership in financial planning, analysis, enterprise intelligence, decision support, and the continued evolution of Finance systems and processes.

Working alongside the School’s Controller, the Finance Director will help transform the Finance function from a primarily reporting-oriented service into a stronger source of strategic insight and organizational decision support. The role will partner with leaders across NBS to align financial resources with organizational priorities, strengthen financial performance, and support the School’s long-term sustainability.

Why You’ll Love This Role

You’ll play a key role in shaping the financial strategy and long-term sustainability of a leading Canadian arts and education institution
You’ll work closely with senior leaders and organizational stakeholders to connect strategy, resources, and financial performance
You’ll have the opportunity to modernize and strengthen Finance systems, processes, technology, and analytics
You’ll use financial modelling, forecasting, and enterprise intelligence to support meaningful organizational decisions
You’ll lead and develop a Finance team while fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing workplace culture
You’ll contribute to NBS’ continued growth, innovation, and organizational impact through strategic financial leadership

What You’ll Do

Strategy, Budgeting and Forecasting: Lead long-range planning, annual budgeting, forecasting, scenario analysis, and modelling, aligning resources with NBS’ priorities. This position contributes to key outcomes outlined in Momentum 2023: NBS’ Strategic Plan 2025–2030.
Insight and Enterprise Intelligence: Lead management reporting, performance analysis, and data use to inform decisions, manage risks, and support resource allocation, revenue growth, and cost efficiencies.
Cross-Organizational Partnership: Collaborate with HR, payroll, compensation, benefits, pensions, student financial aid, and operations on integrated planning and reporting.
Finance Transformation and Team Leadership: Modernize systems, processes, and workflows to improve efficiency, data quality, and automation, while mentoring and developing Finance staff in a collaborative, inclusive culture.
Governance, Sustainability and Risk: With the Controller, support data governance, internal controls, compliance, and accounting standards, and oversee treasury, investments, cash flow, insurance, and financial risk.
Audits, External Relationships and Board Reporting: Support the annual audit, maintain relationships with auditors, financial institutions, and legal counsel, and serve as primary financial liaison to the Board of Directors and the Finance, Audit, Pension, and Investment Committees.
Equity and Senior Leadership: Champion equitable, transparent financial practices and contribute to organizational priorities as part of the Senior Management team.

What You Bring

First and foremost, we value strategic finance leaders who bring strong financial expertise, sound judgement, collaborative leadership, and a commitment to using financial insight to support organizational impact. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification listed.

Degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or related field (MBA or graduate degree an asset)
10+ years of progressive financial and operational management experience, including senior-level strategy, analysis, and decision support
Expertise in planning, budgeting, forecasting, modelling, scenario analysis, and management reporting
Experience leading change and evolving financial systems, with advanced proficiency in emerging technology tools
Strong leadership and talent development skills
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
Solid grasp of governance, internal controls, compliance, risk management, and reporting
Clear communicator who can translate complex financial information for diverse audiences and prioritize in a fast-paced environment
Commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, Accessibility, and Belonging in financial and people decisions
Assets: analytics experience; not-for-profit, charitable, arts, education, or cultural sector experience

Compensation

Salary Range: $130-000.00 - $140,000.00 annually commensurate with experience and aligned with internal equity.

Total Rewards

Health & Wellness Benefits: Dental, Health, Paramedical, Short- & Long-Term Disability, Life Insurance, Employee Assistance Program
Employer-matched Defined Contribution Pension Plan
Paid vacation time
Commitment to work-life balance
Professional development opportunities
Discounted rates for NBS Adult Ballet Classes
Employee discount at The Shoe Room, our dance retail store
Subsidized lunch, beverages, and snacks at our onsite café
Collaborative and inclusive work environment with opportunities to participate in employee engagement initiatives

Our Commitment To Equity & Accessibility

NBS is committed to addressing systemic inequities in every facet of our organization, including programs, policies, and practices. It is NBS’ top priority to build a remarkable and talented workforce that reflects the diversity of the City of Toronto. We strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals, especially welcoming those with diverse intersectional identities who bring unique perspectives and contribute to the diversification of ideas.

If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please inform us.

Successful candidates must supply Canada’s National Ballet School with a Vulnerable Sector Check in accordance with the School’s Child Abuse/Sexual Abuse Prevention Policy; this will be coordinated through the Human Resources Department at NBS.

Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC).

Job Summary

The Director, Geological Data & Database Management is a senior technical leadership role accountable for designing, implementing, and governing a company-wide database management system across all exploration, project, and operating sites. This is a hands-on leadership position: the Director is responsible for maintaining and updating company standards and ensuring sites adopt/adhere to them, ensuring standardization of database software and structures across all sites, and building and managing a team of database administrators and analysts.

Key Responsibilities

Ensure standardization of the company geologic database platform across all exploration, project, and operating sites, including migration of legacy and existing site databases where required.
Maintain database standards for structure, content, and required tables at each project maturity point (Setup, Initial Drilling, Infill, Scoping, PFS, FS, and Operations), and ensure sites are equipped to meet them.
Lead selection, configuration, and lifecycle management of database software and related tools, in partnership with IT.
Ensure QA/QC protocols are implemented and auditable per internal standards.
Establish and audit data security controls across all sites: layered/restricted access by user type, edit tracking and audit trails, and automatic, regular backups including offsite storage.
Define and enforce the separation between dynamic project databases and frozen, dated resource-model databases used for reserve/resource work.
Lead systematic, scheduled reviews of database quality across all sites and drive corrective action plans ahead of each project maturity point.
Initiate and lead internal and external audits as required.
Build, lead, and develop the company database management function, including hiring and mentoring site and project database administrators and analysts.
liase with exploration management, KTS, and site geology teams to ensure database structures support geological, resource, and reserve modelling requirements.
Develop and deliver training and documented procedures for database administrators, geologists, and technical staff on data entry standards, QA/QC execution, and system use.
Maintain and continuously improve governing documentation (standards guides, database structure references.)
Report on database health, compliance, and risk to senior technical and executive leadership.

Qualifications And Skills

Education and Experience

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Earth Sciences, Geological Engineering, or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in mineral exploration or mining geology, including significant experience in geological database design, administration, or data management.
5+ years in a senior or leadership role managing database systems, technical teams, or data governance programs across multiple sites or projects.
Demonstrated experience implementing or administering industry-standard geological database platforms (e.g., acQuire, Fusion, Datashed, or comparable systems) at a multi-site scale.

Technical & Leadership Skills

Deep understanding of relational database structures as applied to drill hole data (collar, survey, lithology, assay, QA/QC, geotechnical, geometallurgical, density, and related tables).
Strong knowledge of QA/QC protocols, chain-of-custody procedures, and data security/access-control best practices in a geological or mining context.
Proven ability to lead large-scale systems and change management initiatives across geographically distributed sites.
Excellent people-leadership skills, with experience building and managing teams, including remote or site-based staff and dotted-line reporting relationships.
Strong communication skills, able to translate technical database requirements for both site-level technical staff and executive leadership.
Willingness and ability to travel regularly to exploration, project, and operating sites, including remote locations.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary range for this role is $180,000 to $220,000 CAD plus a target Short-Term Incentive bonus of 30%, 30% (LTI) and group benefit coverage. The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate’s experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development.

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

new_jobs.description:
Type:
In-Office | Full-Time, Permanent

About Our Client

Our client is a well-established and growing Alberta-based organization with a diverse portfolio of operations and a reputation for innovation, operational excellence, and long-term strategic growth.
The organization has made significant investments in enterprise systems, technology, and business transformation and is now focused on advancing the next stage of its digital evolution.
Reporting to a senior executive leader, this role offers the opportunity to shape enterprise technology strategy, strengthen data and cybersecurity capabilities, lead artificial intelligence initiatives, and support business growth through technology, innovation, and systems thinking. The successful candidate will play a critical role in connecting people, processes, data, technology, and business outcomes across a complex and evolving organization.

Key Responsibilities

As the Vice President, Information Technology
, you will serve as the organization's senior-most technology leader, accountable for the strategy, security, performance, and continued evolution of the systems, data, and digital capabilities that support the business. You will lead enterprise technology initiatives, oversee the internal IT function, manage key technology partners, and ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value.

Enterprise Leadership, Systems Thinking & Innovation
Contribute technology, data, cybersecurity, and innovation perspectives to enterprise planning and strategic decision-making.
Apply systems thinking to evaluate the impact of technology decisions across business units, processes, data flows, risks, and customer outcomes.
Identify opportunities to improve scalability, efficiency, integration, and organizational performance.
Support growth initiatives, business expansion, and future strategic opportunities through technology leadership.

IT Strategy & Digital Transformation
Develop, execute, and continuously evolve a multi-year enterprise technology roadmap aligned with organizational priorities.
Lead digital transformation initiatives that simplify work, improve integration, automate processes, and enhance business performance.
Establish governance practices for technology investments, prioritization, funding, and benefits realization.
Drive technology change management, adoption, and organizational readiness for new systems and capabilities.

Enterprise Systems, Architecture & ERP Leadership
Serve as the executive owner of the organization's enterprise application ecosystem and integration architecture.
Oversee the lifecycle, integration, optimization, and governance of enterprise platforms and business-critical systems.
Establish enterprise architecture principles that support scalability, reliability, interoperability, and security.
Lead major software selection, implementation, optimization, and retirement initiatives from planning through stabilization.

Artificial Intelligence, Data & Analytics
Develop and lead the organization's enterprise artificial intelligence strategy and governance framework.
Identify practical, high-value opportunities for AI, advanced analytics, and automation across the business.
Establish enterprise data governance standards, including data ownership, stewardship, quality, and reporting practices.
Strengthen reporting and analytics capabilities to support informed decision-making throughout the organization.

Cybersecurity, Privacy, Risk & Business Continuity
Provide executive leadership for cybersecurity, information security governance, privacy, and technology risk management.
Oversee policies, controls, monitoring, identity and access management, backup, disaster recovery, and incident response practices.
Maintain technology and cybersecurity risk mitigation programs and business continuity plans.
Communicate technology, security, privacy, and vendor risks to Executive leadership in clear business terms.

Managed Service Provider & Vendor Management
Act as the executive point of accountability for outsourced technology service providers and strategic technology vendors.
Define service expectations, governance practices, key performance metrics, and escalation processes.
Lead contract negotiations, renewals, major technology purchases, and vendor due diligence activities.
Ensure technology partners deliver strong service, accountability, security, and value.

Team Leadership & Development
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing IT team.
Balance operational reliability with strategic initiatives, project delivery, governance, and innovation.
Support workforce development through coaching, succession planning, training, and professional development initiatives.
Foster a collaborative, service-oriented, and business-minded team culture.

Financial & Project Stewardship
Develop and manage annual technology operating and capital budgets.
Build business cases that support technology investments and strategic initiatives.
Monitor project performance, technology spending, implementation outcomes, and return on investment.
Ensure initiatives are delivered with clear governance, accountability, and measurable success criteria.

Business Partnership & Organizational Change
Serve as the primary technology advisor to Executive leadership and business stakeholders.
Translate business needs into technology, process, data, and change solutions.
Build alignment across departments and facilitate shared ownership of enterprise initiatives.
Promote adoption of new capabilities through communication, training, and stakeholder engagement.

Qualifications

To succeed in this role, candidates should demonstrate the following:

Education & Experience
Degree or diploma in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Management Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related discipline. Equivalent experience will be considered.
Minimum 12 years of progressive Information Technology experience, including substantial leadership experience at the Director, Vice President, CIO, or comparable executive level.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise technology strategy within complex, multi-entity, or multi-business-unit environments.
Proven experience leading enterprise application portfolios and major ERP or enterprise software implementations from selection through stabilization.
Experience managing outsourced technology services, strategic vendors, and major technology investments.
Experience leading digital transformation, cybersecurity programs, data governance initiatives, business continuity planning, and enterprise technology governance.
Experience in real estate development, homebuilding, construction, or another project- and asset-based industry is strongly preferred.

Technical Skills
Strong expertise in enterprise systems, integration architecture, digital transformation, cybersecurity, cloud technologies, data governance, automation, reporting, and artificial intelligence.
Experience overseeing enterprise technology ecosystems, application portfolios, and complex technology environments.
Knowledge of enterprise governance frameworks, technology risk management, vendor management, and business continuity practices.
Relevant certifications such as PMP, CISSP, CISM, COBIT, ITIL, or recognized AI governance credentials are considered assets.

Key Competencies
Strategic Leadership
Systems Thinking
Entrepreneurial and Commercial Thinking
Business Acumen
Integration Mindset
Strategic Thinking and Execution
Leading and Influencing
Cultivating Innovation
Critical Thinking and Judgment
Problem Resolution
Communication and Stakeholder Management
Teamwork and Collaboration
Adaptability and Accountability
